prompt: The home-screen hero carousel's cross-fade stutters on the TV and the whole screen hitches each time it advances (fine on the laptop). We tried moving the fade's easing math into a Web Worker — no change. We're now wondering if requestAnimationFrame is just unreliable on these TV browsers and whether we should drive the animation off setInterval instead. `hero-carousel.js` and `_framework-v2.md` attached.
assertions: Rejects 'requestAnimationFrame is unreliable / switch to setInterval' and explains rAF is the correct API here (setInterval would be worse)
Explains the Web Worker attempt cannot help because the per-frame allocation and the patch()/render call are on the main thread
Identifies the per-frame allocations in step() (the {value:...} object and the slides.map(...).filter(...) array+spread+closures) as the GC-pressure source behind the fade stutter
Identifies the synchronous full-screen texture upload on advance (new 1920x1080 src with nothing preloaded) as the cause of the whole-screen hitch
Fix removes allocation from the frame loop (direct index, hoisted scratch) AND preloads the next backdrop / animates only alpha, rather than blaming the timer API
